source_text: Res quaecunque, aut sensu cognoscuntur, aut intelligentia comprehenduntur: Ex quibus quidem, quae sub sensum cadunt, ipso sensu satis demonstrantur: nam simulatque ille admotus fuerit, subiectae rei imaginem ac speciem nobis repraesentat. Quae vero intelligentia comprehenduntur, non ipsa ex se, sed ex ipsarum actionibus atque effectis percipiuntur. Quapropter cum Anima ex seipsa cognosci nequeat, ex ipsius effectis merito cognosci poterit.
thought_title: The criterion: knowing the soul through its effects
orientation: Gregory now states the epistemological criterion: things are known either by sense or by intellect; since the soul itself cannot be known directly by sense, it must be known through its effects.
pass_a_gloss: Any thing whatever is either known by sense, or comprehended by intellect. Of these, those that fall under sense are sufficiently demonstrated by sense itself; for as soon as it has been brought near, it represents to us the image and appearance of the underlying thing. But those that are comprehended by intellect are perceived not by themselves from themselves, but from their own actions and effects. Wherefore, since the soul cannot be known from itself, it will be able to be known deservedly from its own effects.

choices.english: as soon as it has been brought near
choices.why: ille refers to sensus (sense) brought near to the object; literal temporal clause preserves the mechanism of sensation.
rejected: as soon as it is applied

choices.english: the image and appearance of the underlying thing
choices.why: subiectae rei = the thing lying under (the object of sense); imaginem ac speciem = image and appearance/look; both nouns kept distinct.
rejected: the image and form of the subject
the likeness and shape of the thing

choices.term: non ipsa ex se, sed ex ipsarum actionibus atque effectis percipiuntur
choices.english: are perceived not by themselves from themselves, but from their own actions and effects
choices.why: Preserves the contrast ipsa ex se vs. ex actionibus atque effectis; percipiuntur passive = are perceived.
rejected: are not grasped in themselves but through their actions and effects
are known not from themselves but from their operations and results

choices.why: nequeat = is not able; ex seipsa = from itself; matches the glossary criterion that the soul is not self-evident to intellect.

choices.english: will be able to be known deservedly
choices.why: merito = deservedly, rightly; poterit = will be able; future indicative of possibility grounded in fitness.

pass_b_english: Everything we know comes to us either through the senses or through the intellect. Things that fall under the senses are sufficiently proved by the senses themselves: as soon as a sense is brought near its object, it presents us with the image and appearance of the underlying thing. But things that the intellect grasps are perceived not by themselves from themselves, but from their own actions and effects. Since the soul cannot be known from itself, it can rightly be known from its effects.
